text:
Eetu Luostarinen has 4 points in 18 games, and you will not find a Panthers coach who cares much. He's one of the league's best quiet defensive forwards: Evolving-Hockey had him in the 91st percentile at taking chances away last season, against competition in the 94th percentile. Florida takes 57% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice at five on five this year, seven points better than without him.

The scoring has been thin. He has 0.6 individual expected goals over his last ten games against a usual 1.7, and his points rate of 0.83 per 60 minutes is below his range. Sunday in Boston he played only 11:18, the low point of a back-to-back weekend.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking notes a signature worth watching: 24% of his setups come from behind the net, three times the rate of a typical forward. Goalies have to turn and find the puck on those. He's won two Cups with Florida and played for Finland at the Olympics. We project about 13 goals. His line with Anton Lundell and Sandis Vilmanis has taken 66% of the expected goals together; that's the number that keeps him in the lineup.
headline: Luostarinen's job isn't points
